resources.string: Fork bomb — will exhaust system resources.
Recursive force delete — irreversible data loss.
Recursive delete of a broad path — irreversible data loss.
Writes directly to a disk device — can destroy the filesystem.
Pipes a downloaded script straight into a shell — runs unverified remote code.
Pipes output into an interpreter — runs constructed or remote code.
Mirror delete — wipes files in the destination that are absent from the source.
Powers off or reboots the machine.
Recursive permission/ownership change on a system path.
Overwrites a security-critical file.
Flushes firewall rules — may cut off remote access.
Deletes files.
Terminates running processes.
Uninstalls packages.
Discards local changes or rewrites history.
Grants world-writable permissions.
Stops or disables a service.
Bulk-deletes matched files.
Discards file contents.
Runs with elevated privileges.
Exceeds what the guard reads — part of this input was not classified.
